scores.reason: FIB-4, elastography and glucose/HbA1c already drive the pathway and define the cardiometabolic criteria; the Delphi consensus drops HOMA-IR from the criteria for cost and between-laboratory variability. scores.reason: Measure: fasting C-peptide (MMTT-stimulated not evidenced). The only retrieved comparison is a single-centre case-control (44 pancreatogenic vs 35 T2D, fasting C-peptide 0.81 vs 1.71 nmol/L); consensus (PancreasFest 2012) diagnoses 3c without C-peptide and no 3c cutoff was retrieved. No evidence that C-peptide changes TPIAT or treatment decisions. Case-series level.
sources: PMID 23890130 PancreasFest 2012 and PMID 28860126 abstracts (per project files)

scores.reason: Glucose/HbA1c/OGTT, exocrine tests and imaging define type 3c in the consensus; C-peptide adds a documented-deficiency and pre-TPIAT reserve question only by mechanism, with no reclassification data. Alternative bin 2 (useful in the pre-TPIAT subgroup) if a TPIAT study shows C-peptide changes candidate selection; not found in the screened records.

Measure: serum C-peptide, glucose/C-peptide ratio and urinary C-peptide/creatinine ratio (UCPCR). Observational data only: UCPCR <=1.13 nmol/g gave 88% sensitivity and 95% specificity for severe deficiency in 85 T2D patients (single centre, cutoff derived in the same sample, no external validation) and glucose/C-peptide ratio varies with eGFR. No guideline on CKD adjustment and no decision-impact study; the use is a limit on interpretation.

scores.reason: UCPCR avoids the renal clearance problem but is itself a C-peptide measure; whether it beats clinical features, antibodies, or serum C-peptide with eGFR adjustment for the decision was not tested in the retrieved data. Marginal; not determinable beyond that.

Measure: fasting insulin (>30 uU/mL, JDS) plus antibodies and genetics. Single-nation expert criteria without sensitivity or specificity; the lipodystrophy guideline uses insulin requirement as a clinical clue and names no insulin threshold. No study tests insulin-guided testing against usual care.

scores.reason: In the JDS criteria fasting insulin is the only biochemical major sign, so within severe-IR work-up there is no biochemical alternative before antibody or genetic testing; mechanism and criteria only, capped at 2 by clarification 19. Weakness: 89 Japanese T2D adults with BMI <25 had none above 30 and some genetic cases fall below 30.

scores.reason: Insulin and C-peptide suppression is the branch point that separates NICTH from hyperinsulinism within a hypoglycaemia work-up; beta-hydroxybutyrate and glucagon response are partial alternatives from the same fast. Mechanism and case reports only (cap 2); the decisive confirmatory test is IGF-II, not insulin. Alternative bin 1 if the reader treats suppression as only a rule-out.

scores.reason: Scored for part (b), first-trimester fasting HOMA-IR to predict GDM (part (a) is glucose-based). Several cohorts give accuracy data (AUC 0.73 in n=1343; 0.81 in n=250 with 20 cases) with ROC cutoffs that differ by study and BMI (1.43 to 2.27, 2.08, 1.52), so this is prediction, not decision impact; no trial shows HOMA-IR-guided care improves outcomes.

HOMA-IR stayed independent of BMI and weight gain in one logistic model (PMID 26754418), but no delta C-statistic, NRI or calibration against a clinical-risk model, and HbA1c/fasting glucose and BMI alternatives were not compared head to head. Data-driven cutoffs without external validation. Marginal.

scores.reason: Measure: urinary or serum C-peptide (fasting and after glucagon or meal). The cutoffs are criterion 3 of Japanese national expert criteria; no sensitivity or specificity was read; supporting data are small case series (8 patients in one Chinese series with lower C-peptide than classic T1D) and single case reports. No Western guideline cutoff found in the screened records.

scores.reason: Near-normal HbA1c and negative islet antibodies are the other criteria, but only C-peptide documents near-total beta-cell loss; this is definitional and no accuracy comparison exists, so capped at 2. Management (insulin, DKA care) is the same without the label, which limits the added value.

anchor_issues: Row 35: the row mixes (a) a glucose-based GCK trigger and (b) first-trimester HOMA-IR. I scored (b), the only insulin use; (a) would not be an insulin or C-peptide use.

Row 28: the use is an interpretation limit, not a decision; D2 scored on accuracy evidence that C-peptide can be interpreted in CKD (2), noted as a limit on rows 6 to 11.
Row 12 and row 21 D8: 'within the population' alternatives are partial (antibodies, genetics; beta-hydroxybutyrate, IGF-II); both capped at 2 since no reclassification data.
